input.content: Pattern: a "simplification" that drops an ownership/identity guard before deleting shared state. In cleanup_setup(store, workspace_id, setup_id), the simplified code does `store.active.pop(workspace_id, None)` unconditionally, but store.active[workspace_id] records which setup_id owns it ({"setup_id":..., "connection":...}). Per README, cleanup of a failed setup must remove only "any association it owns". In the documented serialized interleaving (setup A fails -> cleanup A queued; setup B begins+completes for same workspace -> active[w] now owned by B; queued cleanup A runs), the unconditional pop silently destroys B's valid completed connection. Correct form guards on identity: association = store.active.get(workspace_id); if association and association["setup_id"] == setup_id: store.active.pop(workspace_id, None). The happy-path unit test (begin one / complete one / cleanup one) passes and masks the bug — green implementation-shaped tests do not prove the documented recovery path. Review lesson: when reviewing a "cleanup"/"simplification", reconstruct the documented interleaving and check whether an identity guard was collapsed away.
